To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the data model and the query model for streaming geospatial image data must be designed in such a way that they are able to support the specific needs of geospatial data, (ii) the query language should provide the user with the ability to specify queries in an intuitive and declarative way and, at the same time, allow for efficient and scalable query processing techniques.

(1) the data model is the most important factor for performance of the query processing algorithms; (2) the query model and its associated operators are the second most important factor; and (3) the performance of the query algorithms is highly dependent on the underlying data structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a data and query model for streaming geospatial image data.
the following questions:  What is a suitable data model for the representation of streaming image data and how is it related to traditional spatial data models?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current research on data stream processing and continuous querying has not been able to address the problem of continuous querying of geospatial image data in a satisfactory way.
the data model is not the problem.
there is no one-size-fits-all data model for geospatial image data, but a variety of models, each of them being appropriate for different applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a new data model, the Geospatial Data Model (GDM) for representing and querying raster image data.
we developed a query model and a query processing framework that is capable of handling complex types of data streams.
the data and query model we propose for streaming geospatial image data is a combination of the relational data model with the raster data model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relational data model is too limited in the sense that it cannot represent complex data objects in a compact and efficient manner.

the data model for streaming geospatial images must support the following features: (1) a data type for representing geospatial images, (2) a data type to support efficient spatial indexing of images, and (3) efficient support for continuous queries over geospatial images.

it is possible to adapt existing query operators to handle such data types, thus allowing for a seamless integration of complex objects into the query processing framework of data stream management systems.
